title: audit-exporter: add destination config schema + validation (Splunk/Datadog/S3)
author: Benji Okafor
body: Context: The audit-export worker needs a stable, strongly-validated destination config shape before we wire up the control plane and UI. This PR introduces a versioned destination configuration schema (v1alpha) for Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, and S3, along with load/validate helpers, sample configs, and unit tests. Summary of changes: Adds DestinationConfigV1Alpha with destination_type enum (splunk_hec|datadog_logs|s3) and per-type config blocks; introduces SecretRef (provider=env|file|kms_placeholder) so we can avoid committing plaintext tokens/keys in config; implements validation with clear error messages (field-level) and safe defaults; adds sample YAML configs under config/samples/ for each sink; adds unit tests covering happy paths and common misconfigurations (missing required fields, invalid URLs, non-HTTPS endpoints, invalid bucket names, unsupported Datadog site, etc.). Notes: This is intentionally not final API surface for the control plane; it’s the internal worker-side schema/contract we’ll map to. We’re keeping it versioned to allow evolution without breaking private installs. Follow-ups: (1) Wire SecretRef to real secret stores in private installs (K8s secret + optional KMS) (2) Extend validation once ADRs land for batching limits and partitioning rules (3) Add schema examples to customer docs once we stabilize field names.
commits: config: introduce v1alpha destination schema + typed structs
validation: add per-sink validators and friendly error formatting
tests: add unit tests for config parsing + validation matrix
conversation: 2025-01-14 10:22 Benji Okafor (author): Adds initial destination config schema + validation. Goal is to unblock connector work with a strict contract and to ensure we don’t accept configs that will later fail deep in the delivery loop. Includes sample YAMLs for local/dev and unit tests. 2025-01-14 12:05 Kevin Osei (reviewer): +1 on versioning. Two asks: (1) can we enforce https only for Splunk/Datadog endpoints by default? (2) avoid allowing plaintext tokens/keys in config even in samples; Security is going to point to this file in reviews. 2025-01-14 12:31 Benji Okafor (author): Good call. I’ll enforce https scheme and update samples to use SecretRef (env) so no tokens are present. For local dev, folks can set SPLUNK_HEC_TOKEN / DATADOG_API_KEY env vars. 2025-01-14 13:10 Hanae Suzuki (reviewer): For SecretRef, can you clarify provider semantics? If provider=env, do we allow missing env var at load time or only at validate time? Also please ensure error messages don’t echo secret values (even if someone mistakenly sets token inline). 2025-01-14 13:46 Benji Okafor (author): Implemented provider enum and moved resolution into load step; validation fails if env var is missing. Added redaction to error formatting (we never print actual values; we print ref name only). Also added a guard: if someone sets token/api_key directly, validation rejects unless allow_insecure_plaintext_secrets=true (default false; only used in test fixtures). 2025-01-14 15:18 Allison Grant (reviewer): Minor: can we standardize naming for datadog “site” vs “endpoint”? We’ll be emitting metrics tags like sink_site=us1, so “site” makes sense. Also please cap string sizes (index/prefix/etc.) to avoid pathological configs. 2025-01-14 16:02 Benji Okafor (author): Kept “site” and added length limits (prefix <= 256, splunk index <= 128, source/sourcetype <= 256). Added tests for boundary cases. 2025-01-15 09:07 Marcus Lin (reviewer): Thanks. Re-ran CI. 2025-01-15 11:20 CI: all checks passed. 2025-01-16 09:14 Kevin Osei (reviewer): Approved. Thanks for the https + secret handling changes. 2025-01-16 09:30 Hanae Suzuki (reviewer): Approved. Redaction logic looks good. 2025-01-16 10:05 Marcus Lin (reviewer): Approved. release_notes: Internal: audit-exporter now has a versioned destination config schema (v1alpha) with strict validation for Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, and S3; sample configs and unit tests included.
